messages:
Anna (CFO): Quick heads up — we're rolling out a tiered rate ladder and an invoice cutover for usage effective 2026-06-15. This affects token pricing bands and the cadence for monthly invoices.
Kevin (Growth): Is this the thing that changes burst credit behavior too?
Anna (CFO): Short answer: yes. Burst credits are being consolidated into a single 'buffer' allocation per account instead of route-level credits. That makes metering simpler and reduces edge-case refunds.
Maya (Support Lead): What do we need to tell customers who are mid-contract?
Tom (Legal): For enterprise contracts with fixed-rate clauses, we honor existing pricing until renewal. We'll reach out to affected customers with legal-approved language.
Chris (Product): Rollout plan: Phase 1 (2026-05-20) — internal preview + console banner. Phase 2 (2026-06-01) — opt-in for early adopters. Phase 3 (2026-06-15) — enforced cutover.
Anna (CFO): Operational notes: invoices generated before midnight UTC on 2026-06-15 use legacy banding. Anything after uses the new ladder. Expect two invoice formats during the transition window.
billing-bot: Reminder: automated billing export will switch schema on 2026-06-15. See /billing/schema-migration for the CSV field map.
Kevin (Growth): Any credits/offsets for startups who rely on burst credits heavily?
Anna (CFO): We're applying a one-time transition credit to qualifying Startup and Growth accounts. The eligibility criteria will be in the customer email.
Maya (Support Lead): Support playbook incoming — will include canned responses, refund rules, and escalation matrix. ETA: 2026-05-22.
Chris (Product): Technical impact: rate-limiting middleware will adopt a per-customer ladder that changes effective token rate based on 30d consumption. No API key rotation required.
Maya (Support Lead): Will customers see rate-limit headers change?
Chris (Product): Yes — headers will include `x-rate-tier` and `x-tier-window` after the preview. We'll document sample responses.
Tom (Legal): Please do not promise retroactive refunds in outreach messaging. Use 'transition credits' and 'one-time adjustment' phrasing.
Anna (CFO): Finance tasks: update invoice templates, ensure tax calc unchanged, notify collections. Finance will run a dry-run billing pass on 2026-06-10 for internal validation.
Kevin (Growth): Do we have a simple customer-facing FAQ for the console banner?
Chris (Product): Draft FAQ is at https://redwood.internal/announcements/rate-ladder-faq (internal only). Highlights: why, effective date, examples, contact channels.
Maya (Support Lead): Will we need extra headcount on support on cutover day? Likely yes — recommend on-call rotation supplemented by billing SMEs.
Anna (CFO): We approved limited overtime budget for June 15-17 for support and finance.
billing-bot: Action item created: `billing-migration/dry-run-2026-06-10` assigned to FinanceOps.
Kevin (Growth): Suggested comms: personalized emails to top 50 customers, in-console banner, and in-product modal for heavy users.
Tom (Legal): Approving two templates: Enterprise and General. Sending to comms for personalization.
Maya (Support Lead): Noted — will add escalation contact and sample refund calc to the playbook.
Anna (CFO): Final ask: teams, review the preview console banner and sample invoice by 2026-05-25. I'll schedule a 30-min sync for 2026-05-26 to capture any late blockers.
Kevin (Growth): Thanks — I can co-host the customer outreach call.
Chris (Product): Will post the preview build link tomorrow.
Anna (CFO): Appreciate the quick turnaround team. :heart:
Maya (Support Lead): +1 — thanks everyone.
billing-bot: Thread archived for action tracking.
